profile.receptive: B2 — strong at extracting main ideas from paraphrased passages and recognising formal business/polite vocabulary (afford, inconvenience).
profile.productive: A2+–B1 — communicates ideas clearly, but drops auxiliary/linking verbs under cognitive load and tends to write single-sentence answers instead of 3–5 sentence paragraphs.
profile.languages: Native/fluent in Turkish and Uyghur (Arabic script).
profile.interests: Learns best through video tutorials combined with hands-on building and troubleshooting (e.g. technical Minecraft mods: Create, Mekanism, Modern Industrialization). Values practical, real-world fluency and structured step-by-step feedback.
profile.goal: CEFR B1 → confident B2 in reading, speaking, listening and writing.

modules.title: Core Clause Structure & Auxiliary Verbs
modules.focus: Eliminating dropped be (am/is/are) and have/had; Present Simple vs Continuous; top irregular verbs (drive–drove–driven).

modules.title: Gerunds, Infinitives & Used To Patterns
modules.focus: used to + V1 (past habits), be used to + V-ing (familiarity), get used to + V-ing (adapting); verb + preposition patterns.

modules.title: High-Frequency Everyday Phrasal Verbs
modules.focus: put off vs call off, come up, figure out, look into, turn down, catch up; separable pronoun order.

modules.title: Conditionals & Hypothetical Thinking
modules.focus: Zero, 1st, 2nd and 3rd conditionals (If I knew… vs If I had known…); past modals of deduction (must/should/might have).

modules.title: Structured Paragraph Writing
modules.focus: Expanding 1-sentence replies into cohesive 4–5 sentence paragraphs: topic sentences, connectors (furthermore, however, as a result), punctuation.

modules.title: B2 Fluency & Register Control
modules.focus: Shifting between casual conversation and professional writing with idioms, collocations and nuanced B2 vocabulary.

next: Eliminating dropped have / had auxiliaries in Present Perfect & Past Perfect sentences, plus high-frequency irregular verbs in everyday storytelling.

homework.prompt: What is one skill or subject you are currently trying to improve, and what hands-on method helps you keep track of your progress?
checklist: A complete finite verb (am/is/are…) in every clause

patterns.title: Dropped linking/auxiliary be (is / are)
patterns.wrong: Watching videos [is] more effective because when you [are] learning…
patterns.right: Watching videos is more effective because when you are learning…
patterns.rule: Every English clause needs a finite verb: is/are before adjectives, am/is/are before -ing verbs.

patterns.title: Separable phrasal verb pronoun order
patterns.wrong: I felt I figured out it.
patterns.right: I felt I figured it out.
patterns.rule: Object pronouns go between verb and particle: figure it out, pick it up, put it off.

patterns.title: Time duration with take
patterns.wrong: It took my lots of time to figure out…
patterns.right: It took me a lot of time to figure out…
patterns.rule: Use an object pronoun after take + duration: It took me two hours.

patterns.title: Transitive verb cause (no 'to')
patterns.rule: cause + direct object (compare: lead to mistakes).

patterns.title: Reflexive pronoun agreement
patterns.wrong: …by watching videos and making it oneself.
patterns.right: …by watching videos and making it myself.
patterns.rule: Match the reflexive to the subject: I → myself, you → yourself.

patterns.title: drive vs derive
patterns.wrong: Today she derived because of the rain.
patterns.right: Today she is driving because of the rain.
patterns.rule: drive–drove–driven; derive = to obtain from a source.

patterns.title: put off vs call off
patterns.wrong: …call off the meeting until next Tuesday.
patterns.right: …put off the meeting until next Tuesday.
patterns.rule: put off = postpone; call off = cancel completely.

patterns.title: 3rd conditional auxiliary had
patterns.wrong: If I known you were coming…
patterns.right: If I had known you were coming…
patterns.rule: If + had + V3, would have + V3.

patterns.title: be used to + gerund
patterns.wrong: …now I am used to hear it.
patterns.right: …now I am used to hearing it.
patterns.rule: to is a preposition here, so -ing follows.

patterns.title: Paragraph length & introductory comma
patterns.wrong: If I forget something I… (one-sentence answer)
patterns.right: If I forget something, I… (3–4 connected sentences)
patterns.rule: Comma after an introductory if-clause; expand 1-sentence answers into 3–4 connected sentences.
